blocks.content: There shall be a President of India.

items: Nominated members of Parliament do NOT participate in the presidential election, but they DO participate in the impeachment process.
Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies participate in the election, but they DO NOT participate in the impeachment process.

An impeachment resolution under Article 61 requires a 14-day notice signed by at least 1/4th of the initiating House's total membership and must be passed by a special majority of 2/3rd of total membership of each House.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 52 mandates that there shall be a President of India, who serves as the executive head of the State.
The President is indirectly elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies.
Qualifications under Article 58 mandate Indian citizenship, a minimum age of 35 years, and eligibility for election to the Lok Sabha.
The Oath of Office is administered by the Chief Justice of India under Article 60.
The President can only be impeached under Article 61 on the specific ground of 'violation of the Constitution'.
